measured.trade_shape: 0.5 ATR stop on ES is roughly 35 points = $175 at one micro, 17.5% of the $1,000 buffer; 2R target is +$350
measured.note: day_shape measured on all 2494 sessions: the rule fires 43.8% of the time, so most days are flat. A $500 day happened 17 times in ten years at one micro (0.68%); a $200 day 5.1%. The win rate and pass rate above are the causal figures, not the retracted legacy ones.

retracted.why: RESEARCH-LOG (t) and (v). The legacy sweep still reproduces them on the same bars: 84.8% win and a 96% pass rate, from the same rule, purely by resolution.

size_rule: One micro. The stop is 0.5 ATR narrowed to a $250 fixed ceiling (50 ES points), so the dollars at risk do not grow with volatility and no signal is refused for being wide. 2R target = $500. Two micros would put $500 at risk on one trade, which is twice what this leg has measured.
why_this_one: It is the highest measured pass rate of any configuration whose order type can actually be placed (59%), it trades 0.18 times a session so it will actually fire, and a 2R target only needs 30.8% wins to break even rather than the 67.6% that 0.5R demanded.
what_is_not_proven: No daily-bar rule in this repo has a statistically separable edge once 3,584 configurations are corrected for and index drift is removed. The best surviving line earns $2.49 per session at one micro. This book is the best of a weak field, not a known winner.
kill_rule: Two consecutive full stops (-$350) or -$700 in a session: stop for the day and log it. A breach of the trailing floor ends the attempt, not the research.

book_review_2026_11_22.measured: risknorm.py, 2023-01-01 to 2026-11-20, one micro, causal resolution, session lock and 50% rule. Alone: 421 trades, 55% win, +$27.91/trade, pass 64.6%, breach 18.7%, worst day -$301, max DD -$1,692, 63 median sessions. Drift null (weekday-matched random longs, 100 draws): alpha +$28.16/trade, t +3.90.
book_review_2026_11_22.why: It is the only leg with a positive forward record, the only one whose edge beats its own random-entry null, and the only configuration that improves BOTH the pass rate and the breach rate over the book it replaced. The $300 cap stays exactly as adopted in (xix); this leg is simply the one allowed to use it.
book_review_2026_11_22.one_leg: Every two-leg book measured on the same walk is worse than this leg alone: ES+GC 46.2% pass / 39.3% breach, ES+NQ 31.4% / 38.2%, ES+CL+GC 57.7% / 32.4%. The reason is the 50% consistency add-on: two correlated dip-buyers can bank $800-$1,100 in one session, which needs $1,600-$2,200 of profit to be eligible. Single-leg books had a 0% consistency failure rate.

measurement_2026_11_22: risknorm.py, 2023+ one micro, causal fills, $400 lock, 50% rule. skip $300: 421 trades, 64.6% pass, 18.7% breach, +$27.91/trade. fixed $250 ceiling: 453 trades, 63.6% pass, 19.7% breach, +$30.63/trade, worst day -$301, max DD -$1,754, median 63 sessions. The two are within noise of each other; the fixed ceiling is taken because it always trades -- on 2026-11-22 the skip policy refused a $432 order for the seventh session in a row.

why_this_one: Booked so the desk always trades at the open. The prior-low limit fills only 43.8% of sessions, so a Monday can pass with nothing settled; this leg fires on 98.9% of sessions because it takes the direction of the gap at the open. Its measured expectation is negative, which is why it is one micro and labelled research: the point is forward data, not profit.
